composition_label: Product comparison (Smart product search): Attribute normalization, side-by-side comparison and preference ranking

construction.implementation_origin: New implementation authored directly in the isolated build directory; no other build or repository files read or copied.

input.fixture_label: Required nonempty text. Example is explicitly synthetic.
input.attributes: 1..30 objects: id, label, type (number/text/boolean); optional unit and aliases list (0..20). Attribute ids and aliases are whitespace-normalized and casefolded, globally unique.
input.products: 2..50 objects: unique case-sensitive nonempty id, nonempty name, attributes object. Attribute keys accept declared aliases. Absent or null values are missing. Unknown keys and duplicate canonical values are rejected.
input.preferences: 1..30 objects: attribute, mode, positive finite numeric weight; value required for target/equals, prohibited for higher/lower. Each canonical attribute appears at most once. Numeric modes require numeric attributes.

success_output.fixture_label: Input fixture label with whitespace normalized
success_output.normalized_products: Input product order preserved; attributes contain every declared canonical key, canonical scalar values or null.
success_output.comparison: product_order plus rows in attribute declaration order. Each row includes attribute, label, type, unit or null, and product-id-to-value mapping.
success_output.ranking: Descending score, then case-sensitive product id; sequential rank, product_id, score and per-preference contributions with attribute/mode/missing/score/weighted_score.

shared_schema.validation: One shared validate function checks structure, rejects unknown fields and normalizes products and preference values before comparison/ranking. JSON loader also rejects duplicate keys and nonfinite constants. Finite overflow checks cover conversions. No third-party validation library.
shared_schema.cli: Exactly one input path. UTF-8 JSON input; exactly one JSON output object. Exit 0 on success; exit 2 for file, parsing or validation errors.

cross_stage_handoffs: JSON object -> shared validation -> canonical attribute definitions, normalized product records and normalized preferences
Normalized product records -> side-by-side attribute rows without additional transformations
Same normalized product records and preferences -> weighted scoring contributions -> deterministic ranking
Comparison rows, normalized products and ranking -> one versioned success output

normalization: Text values: collapse whitespace and casefold. Boolean values: native booleans or case-insensitive true/false/yes/no strings.
Numeric values: finite JSON numbers or numeric strings with optional unit suffix; bare values use the attribute's declared unit.
Supported mass units: g, kg, oz, lb. Length: mm, cm, m, in. Decimal storage: MB, GB, TB (1000-based). Currency: USD only.

Convert compatible numeric units to declared canonical units. Unit labels are case-insensitive. No currency exchange; incompatible/unknown units rejected. Unitless numeric attributes cannot accept unit suffixes.
ranking: Missing preference values score zero and keep their preference weight in the denominator.
Higher/lower: min-max score over nonmissing candidates; equal available values score one.
Equals: exact equality after shared normalization scores one, mismatch zero.
Target: score = 1 / (1 + absolute distance / span). Span is candidate maximum minus minimum; when zero or unavailable, use max(abs(target), 1). Arithmetic is scaled to reduce overflow risk.
Total is the positive-weight average. Weights are scaled by their maximum to avoid summation overflow.

Aggregate scores are rounded to six decimal places before ordering; equal displayed scores sort by product id. Contribution scores are also rounded to six decimals, so displayed contributions may differ slightly from the displayed aggregate when summed.
behavior.determinism: No randomness, clock-dependent results, network access, live providers or LLM step.
behavior.synthetic_example: Imaginary portable computers Alpha, Beta and Gamma; expected ranking alpha (0.566667), gamma (0.5), beta (0.4).

included: Declared attribute aliases and typed normalization
Shared validation, structured errors and runnable CLI
Synthetic examples and standard-library unittest coverage
excluded: External catalog retrieval or search engine
Live pricing, currency exchange or tax calculations
Web UI, persistent database and enterprise deployment
Domain-specific restrictions on negative numeric values

coverage: Synthetic normal comparison, conversions and expected ranking
All values missing and deterministic ties
Invalid scalars, unsupported units and nonfinite values
Invalid schema, aliases, duplicate ids and duplicate canonical attributes
Invalid preference modes, values and weights
Very large finite values and weights
Missing-file, directory and argument CLI failures
Malformed JSON, duplicate keys and nonfinite constants using in-memory fixtures
